items.title: Snow Disrupts Austrian Roads
items.gist: Heavy snow brought traffic and public transport problems across Austria.
items.summary: Heavy snow fell across much of Austria on Thursday. The A21 near Vienna was closed in both directions for a time. Roads in Tirol and other regions also saw closures, crashes and delays. Rail services and buses were affected in some areas. Weather forecasters expected more snow before conditions eased later. Officials urged people to drive carefully and allow extra time.
items.host_open: Austria’s first big snowfall arrived with a very busy traffic report. How has the weather affected your plans?

items.title: Nehammer Denies Press Intervention
items.gist: The former chancellor rejected claims that he tried to influence media coverage.
items.summary: Former Austrian chancellor Karl Nehammer testified on Thursday before a parliamentary inquiry committee. The inquiry concerns the case of former justice official Christian Pilnacek. Nehammer denied trying to influence reporting by ORF or the newspaper Kronen Zeitung. The committee is examining possible political influence and the handling of information about the case. Nehammer gave his account, while committee members are continuing to question witnesses. The inquiry may add to debate about trust in public institutions.
items.host_open: A parliamentary hearing can make old questions feel very current. Did Nehammer’s denial surprise you?

items.title: Israeli Strikes Kill Eight In Gaza
items.gist: Health officials reported deaths after overnight Israeli strikes in Gaza.
items.summary: At least eight people were killed in overnight Israeli strikes in Gaza, according to local health officials. Israel’s military said one strike targeted three militants. It did not immediately comment on another strike, according to the report. The strikes come despite a ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas. Israeli fire and airstrikes have continued during the period since that deal. The deaths underline the danger facing civilians, while key details of the strikes remain disputed or unconfirmed.
items.host_open: Reports from Gaza describe another deadly night. How are you feeling about the continued violence?

items.title: Ukraine Faces Fresh Russian Attacks
items.gist: Both sides reported new attacks as the war continued overnight.
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine reported fresh drone and missile attacks overnight into Thursday. Moscow reported an attack on an industrial area in southern Russia. Kyiv reported damage to civilian buildings, according to Reuters. The reports describe claims from both sides, and details may change as more information becomes available. The attacks came as Russia’s war against Ukraine continues. They add to concerns about the safety of civilians and infrastructure.
items.host_open: The overnight reports show how quickly the war can reach far from the front. How does this news look from Austria?

items.title: EU Debates Major Ukraine Loan
items.gist: European leaders are divided over a proposed loan and the bloc’s future budget.
items.summary: EU leaders met in Brussels to discuss the bloc’s long-term budget. They also considered a new loan of about 45 billion euros for Ukraine. The money would help cover economic and military needs next year. Some member states oppose using EU funds for military aid. Supporters say backing Ukraine is part of Europe’s shared security. An agreement may take more talks, with diplomats expecting a decision later.
items.host_open: Europe’s budget talks now include a large question about shared responsibility. Does the proposed loan seem like the right approach?

items.title: Judge Blocks FCC Action Against ABC
items.gist: A court ruling halted the regulator’s early review of ABC station licences.
items.summary: A US judge blocked the Federal Communications Commission from pursuing early reviews of licences held by ABC-owned stations. The FCC had ordered the reviews after disputes involving the network and its programming. ABC argued that the action was retaliation for content it broadcast. The ruling is a setback for the regulator’s effort. The case sits within wider legal disputes between the Trump administration and news organisations. The government’s actions and ABC’s objections reflect opposing views about regulation and press freedom.
items.host_open: A court has put a pause on a high-profile media dispute. Did the ruling surprise you?

items.title: Markets Rise During US Holiday
items.gist: European and Asian share markets gained while US markets were closed.
items.summary: Share prices rose in Europe and Asia on Thursday. US stock markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday. Buying of artificial-intelligence-linked shares helped lift some Asian markets. Investors remained cautious about the AI trade and possible new US tariffs. Germany, France and Britain all recorded gains in early trading. US markets were due to reopen on Friday for a shorter session.
items.host_open: With Wall Street taking a holiday, other markets still had a lively day. Did the gains surprise you?

items.title: Thanksgiving Parade Moves To Saturday
items.gist: New York postponed its famous parade because of dangerous weather.
items.summary: New York’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was moved from Thursday to Saturday. Organisers made the decision after consulting city officials about severe weather. Forecasters warned of strong winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding. The city said the conditions could make the large parade balloons unsafe. Some performers and groups confirmed they would still take part on Saturday. Organisers said they were working through the changes to the event.
items.host_open: Even the parade balloons have to wait for calmer weather. Would you still go on Saturday?
